neighbours.label: A position word (left, right, top, center, 'from left') in a photo caption that tells the reader which pictured person or thing is meant; the same words as directions or in other senses stay quiet.
fire: Mayor Linda Park (right) talks with students at the fair.
In this photo, coach Dan Reed, left, speaks with a player.
Members of the board (front row, from left): Joan, Mike and Ed.
Shown here (left to right) are the winners of the bake sale.
The male (bottom) is larger than the female in this species.
Nurse Ellen Cho (center) checks a patient at the clinic.
Senator Hayes, right, shakes hands with a voter.
Pictured above (from left) are Sam, Jill and Rosa.
quiet: Mayor Linda Park has the right idea about the fair.
The coach left after he spoke with a player.
Members of the board left early for the airport.
Turn right at the corner to reach the bake sale.
The bottom of the cage is lined with paper for this species.
The center of town has a clinic for patients.
Senator Hayes was right about the voters.
Keep your left foot on the pedal and turn the wheel.

short: position word in a photo caption
notes: Probes: '(center)' 0.93, ', left,' 0.86, against 'Turn left at the light' 0.10 and 'You are right' 0.01. The output direction promotes ' left', ' middle', ' row', ' shown'.
